reason: Each child glosses one verse line stating which knowledge, which level and which object-range the higher knowledges have, with a brief reason only.
The children raise and answer why only these three are the knowledges and analyse in which sense each is a knowledge of the one beyond training.
The children identify which higher knowledges are the three miracles and gloss the verse line naming the teaching miracle as supreme.
The children give extended analysis of miraculous power, emanation minds, speech of emanations and blessings, with many doubts raised and answered and rival views.
The children discuss the nature of the divine eye and ear, answer a doubt, cite scripture and explain how different persons see.
The children raise and answer doubts about birth-acquired powers and their bases, with a scriptural citation on recalling past lives.
The second child goes beyond a gloss, answering a doubt and setting out divergent Vaibhashika and Sautrantika views on one-pointedness.
The children are short definitions of the first dhyana and of the remaining three by the factors they possess or abandon.
The children are one-line glosses stating how the formless states resemble and differ from the dhyanas.
The four children are single-line definitions of the four formless spheres, splitting one list.
The children argue at length against form existing in the formless realm, cite sutras and resolve a doubt about how form re-arises.
The children raise and answer a doubt about why the formless spheres bear their names and give alternative explanations of the last one.
The children are brief enumerations of the three types of the lower seven absorptions and the two types of the peak of existence.
The first child explains the function of each dhyana factor in detail and records the master's divergent view, beyond simple listing.
The children debate the nature of bliss and mental pleasure in the dhyanas, refuting other schools with scriptural citations.
The children explain which feelings occur in the birth dhyanas and resolve a doubt about seeing, hearing and speech in higher dhyanas.
The children are concise glosses stating how pure, uncontaminated and afflicted absorptions are each obtained.
The children gloss verse lines listing what arises immediately after each of the three kinds of absorption.
The children are brief glosses on what arises at death after pure and afflicted absorptions.
The children enumerate the four concordant types, define each, and list what follows each, as glosses of the verse.
The children describe step by step the distinct procedures of the remote and near preparations for leap-over absorption.
The children are glosses stating the general rule on which basis manifests which absorption and the exception for the peak, each with a brief reason.
The children gloss verse lines stating the object-range of afflicted, pure and formless absorptions with brief reasons.
The children are glosses stating what the uncontaminated main stages and the preparatory stages abandon, with short supporting reasons.
The children are short glosses on the nature, feeling, exception and an alternative view concerning the preparatory stages.
The children briefly identify the special dhyana and give its divisions, feeling and result, mostly in one line each.
The children identify the three samadhis by their aspects, give their division and name them the three doors of liberation.
The five children are mostly one-line specifications of object, nature, basis, person and level of the doubled samadhis.
The children name the four immeasurables, give the reason for their number and briefly define each.
The children are one-line statements of the levels of the immeasurables and of other schools' views on them.
The children are one-line glosses identifying the first two liberations as repulsiveness and stating their levels.
The children briefly identify the cessation liberation and the entering and emerging minds, as glosses of the verse.
The second child goes on to raise and answer why no liberation is placed in the third dhyana and why the beautiful liberation is cultivated in the fourth.
The children are one-line pointers saying the masteries are like the first, second and beautiful liberations.
The children discuss the totalities with several scholars' views, a scriptural citation and a comparison of liberations, masteries and totalities.
The second child raises and answers how formless absorptions arise in the upper realms, explaining the powers of cause and karma at length.
The children are single phrases naming the two kinds of dharma, scripture and realization, splitting one sentence.
The children identify the two holders of the dharma, splitting one sentence; the long discussion of the teaching's duration belongs to the parent topic.
The children give a full word-by-word commentary on the verses about decline and an exhortation to heedfulness backed by several citations.
The children only quote the closing line and the translators' colophon; the author's own concluding verses and colophon belong with the parent.
